messages:
jordan-support: FYI customers reporting spikes of 502/504 on the hosted inference API since the 15:02 deploy. Support queue has 6 escalations (AcmeMobile, Shoply, PixelCart). Error rate ~8% on /v1/generate-main route.

sam-sre: Thanks — can you paste the request ids or a sample error payload? Any pattern on region or model variant?

jordan-support: Sample from AcmeMobile: 
{
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d",
  "status": 502,
  "error": "upstream_timeout"
}
All from us-east-1, main-model-v2. Latency for successful calls also up 2x.

maria-eng: I pushed a canary earlier that toggles the new traffic-segmentation flag (segment_by_bucket=true) to 10% traffic at 15:01. That flag also touches the prefetch/batching routing path.

alex-release: Deploy bot shows: deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.17-canary at 15:01 UTC -> flags: traffic-segmentation=on (canary).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: service: inference-hosted; env: prod; traffic: 10%; users: canary group; commit: a1f4d9d; started: 2026-03-17T15:01:12Z

sam-sre: If the flag touched routing/batching we might see KV cache misses and timeouts. Can you check the shedder/kvcache error rates? Dashboards: https://dash.internal/redwood/inference/latency?range=15m

maria-eng: Checking logs now. I see an increase in kvcache_lookup failures correlated with canary nodes. Query: 

log snippet:
[15:03:04] node-canary-7: kvcache: miss key=seg:abc123 route=main-model-v2
[15:03:04] node-canary-7: batching: flush timeout after 200ms, batch_size=1
[15:03:05] node-canary-7: upstream: connect timeout to transformer-pool

Looks like canary instances are invoking a different kernel path that bypasses warm caches.

ops-oncall: Customer impact confirmed. Paging SRE for rollback approval. Do we have a quick mitigation (reduce canary to 0% or rollback flag)?

alex-release: I can immediately set the canary's traffic to 0% (stop rollout) or flip flag off across canary servers. Which is faster?

sam-sre: Stop rollout (set traffic 0) should be fastest via router-control. Follow runbook section "canary-stop-and-rollback". I will coordinate rollback once we confirm scope.

jordan-support: I'll notify customers we're investigating and offer a short-lived retry/backoff workaround on our side.

maria-eng: Important detail — the flag change included an inadvertent selector change: selector regex used to match canary nodes was too permissive and matched some regional router instances (us-east primary). So traffic wasn't strictly isolated. That explains broader impact.

alex-release: Initiating stop-rollout command: 
```
routerctl stop-rollout --service inference-hosted --rollout-id a1f4d9d
```

deploy-bot: Rollout stop requested by alex-release at 2026-03-17T15:10:21Z. Phase: draining existing canary sessions.

sam-sre: I'm switching fallback policy to fallback-to-stable-model and increasing shedder threshold to prevent queuing. Patching now.

ops-oncall: Can we get a reproduction step from support to validate fix?

jordan-support: Repro steps I gave to engineering: 
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Region: us-east-1" -d '{"model":"main-model-v2","prompt":"hi"}' -v
2) Observe 502/504 with request id header X-Req 

Also provided two failing request_ids above.

maria-eng: After stop-rollout, logs show a drop in kvcache misses on primary nodes. I still see a handful of errors possibly from drained canary sessions.

sam-sre: Recommendation: fully rollback the flag change from the canary config and re-deploy a corrected canary with stricter selector. Create a hotfix to avoid selector-regex defaulting to global.

alex-release: Agree. I'll create rollback PR and run a patch deploy. ETA ~25 minutes. Anyone on-call to approve quick hotfix?

ops-oncall: I'm available. Approve after CI smoke passes. Make sure to notify support and product that we're rolling back.

jordan-support: I'll send a message to affected customers with current mitigation: we stopped the canary rollout and plan a rollback; ETA ~30m. Offering priority queueing until fully resolved.

maria-eng: Quick note — mitigation workaround for clients: adding header X-Prefer-Stable: true routes to stable variant (temporary server-side honor). We can enable that for escalated tenants from the support dashboard.

alex-release: Rollback PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/inference/PR/2187 (patch: revert traffic-segmentation flag change, tighten selector). Tagging ops-oncall for approval.

deploy-bot: CI smoke passed at 2026-03-17T15:30:12Z. Ready to deploy on approval.

ops-oncall: Approving hotfix, proceed with rolling rollback.

deploy-bot: Hotfix deploy started at 2026-03-17T15:34:02Z -> service: inference-hosted; env: prod; change: revert-traffic-segmentation-canary; rollout: immediate small-batch then verify.

maria-eng: Post-rollback metrics: 5xx error rate dropped from ~8% to ~0.6% within 4 minutes. KV cache miss rates back to baseline.

jordan-support: Notifying customers: issue mitigated by stopping canary and rolling back flag; monitoring. Offering refund assessment if customers impacted billing.

sam-sre: Closing triage: root cause = misapplied traffic-segmentation flag with overly-broad selector that caused canary behavior to affect primary routers, leading to KV cache misses and batching timeouts causing upstream timeouts. Actions: 1) Rollback done; 2) Add stricter validation on selector regex in flag UI; 3) Add canary isolation test in preflight; 4) Postmortem + customer comms.

jordan-support: Thanks team. I'll gather customer timelines and attach logs to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
